---
title: "Custom Models and Cumulative Flows"
format: html
---

`SIRModel()` and `SEIRModel()` are convenient starting constructors, but they
are not the whole modelling framework. When your structure needs extra
compartments or custom transitions, `CompartmentModel()` keeps the state and
transition rules explicit.

This tutorial also shows cumulative flows, which are useful when you want
incidence-like event counts alongside the ordinary compartment trajectory.
See [docs/generic_compartment_models.md](../docs/generic_compartment_models.md),
[docs/cumulative_flow_states_design.md](../docs/cumulative_flow_states_design.md),
[docs/epidemic_model_workflows.md](../docs/epidemic_model_workflows.md),
[examples/generic_msir.R](../examples/generic_msir.R),
[examples/deterministic_cumulative_flows.R](../examples/deterministic_cumulative_flows.R),
and [examples/stochastic_cumulative_flows.R](../examples/stochastic_cumulative_flows.R).

```{r}
if ("package:agepi" %in% search()) {
  # Package already available.
} else if (dir.exists("R")) {
  invisible(lapply(list.files("R", pattern = "[.]R$", full.names = TRUE), source))
} else if (requireNamespace("agepi", quietly = TRUE)) {
  library(agepi)
} else {
  stop(
    "Package agepi is not available. Run this tutorial from the package root ",
    "or install agepi first.",
    call. = FALSE
  )
}

age_structure <- AgeStructure(
  age_groups = c("0-4", "5-9", "10+"),
  lower_bounds = c(0, 5, 10),
  upper_bounds = c(4, 9, Inf)
)

contact_matrix <- matrix(
  c(
    4, 2, 1,
    2, 5, 2,
    1, 2, 4
  ),
  nrow = age_structure$n_age_groups,
  byrow = TRUE
)

initial_state <- data.frame(
  compartment = rep(c("M", "S", "I", "R"), each = age_structure$n_age_groups),
  age_group = rep(age_structure$age_groups, times = 4),
  value = c(
    c(100, 20, 0),
    c(890, 1170, 898),
    c(10, 10, 2),
    c(0, 0, 0)
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

model <- CompartmentModel(
  compartments = c("M", "S", "I", "R"),
  infection_transitions = data.frame(from = "S", to = "I", stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
  transitions = data.frame(
    from = c("M", "I"),
    to = c("S", "R"),
    rate = c(0.15, 0.25),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ),
  infectious_compartments = "I"
)

output <- simulate_deterministic(
  initial_state = initial_state,
  times = seq(0, 2, by = 0.1),
  model = model,
  age_structure = age_structure,
  contact_matrix = contact_matrix,
  beta = 0.08,
  method = "euler",
  cumulative_flows = list(
    infections = list(from = "S", to = "I"),
    recoveries = list(from = "I", to = "R")
  )
)

head(output$trajectory, 12)
head(output$cumulative, 12)
cumulative_flow_totals(output$cumulative)
cumulative_flow_totals_wide(output$cumulative)
```

The cumulative output is not a new compartment. It is a separate count of
selected transition events, so it reads like incidence or recovery activity
over time rather than as a state that belongs inside the disease model.

That distinction matters because it keeps the ordinary compartment totals and
the event counts separate. If you want a quick comparison between the two,
`cumulative_flow_totals()` and `cumulative_flow_totals_wide()` are the easiest
inspection helpers.

For the stochastic version of the same idea, see
[examples/stochastic_cumulative_flows.R](../examples/stochastic_cumulative_flows.R).
